'''Caroline Uhler''' (born 1983){{r|start}} is a Swiss statistician working in the field of [[machine learning]] and applications in [[genomics]]. Her research focuses on developing methods for causal inference to infer regulatory relationships from different data modalities (transcriptomic, proteomic, structural, etc.){{r|broad}}. She is a Full Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and the Institute for Data, Systems and Society at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>https://www.carolineuhler.com/</ref> In addition, she is a Core Institute Member at the [[Broad Institute]], where she directs the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center.<ref>https://www.ericandwendyschmidtcenter.org/</ref>

==Education and career==
Uhler was born in Switzerland.{{r|start}} She studied mathematics and biology at the [[University of Zurich]], earning a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 2004, and a second bachelor's degree in biology and master's degree in mathematics in 2006. She stayed at the university for a credential as a high school mathematics teacher in 2007, but instead of becoming a teacher she traveled to the US for graduate education at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. There, she earned both a Ph.D. in statistics and a degree in management of technology from the [[Haas School of Business]] in 2011.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Geometry of maximum likelihood estimation in Gaussian graphical models'', was supervised by [[Bernd Sturmfels]], an [[algebraic geometry|algebraic geometer]] and [[algebraic statistics|algebraic statistician]].{{r|mg}}

She became an assistant professor at the [[Institute of Science and Technology Austria]] in 2012, after a short postdoc at the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]] at the [[University of Minnesota]] as well as at [[ETH Zurich]]. She moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2015 as Henry L. and Grace Doherty Assistant Professor in 2015, and was promoted to associate professor in 2018 and to full professor in 2022.{{r|cv}} Since 2022, Uhler has also been a Core Institute Member at the Broad Institute, where she directs the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ericandwendyschmidtcenter.org/about/leadership | title=Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center &#124; Leadership }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Uhler has received multiple prestigious career prizes: In 2014, Uhler became an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}} In 2015, she was a winner of the [[Start-Preis]] of the [[Austrian Science Fund]],{{r|start}} and of the Sofja Kovalevskaja Award of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]], but declined the funding to move to MIT.{{r|cv}} In 2017, Uhler received the [[NSF Career Award]] and the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]]. In 2019, Uhler became a [[Simons Investigator]] in Mathematical Modeling of Living Systems, and in 2022, she received the [[NIH Director's New Innovator Award]]. She was elected as [[SIAM Fellow]] in 2023.
